title: OpenAI launches Partner Network with $150M fund, 300,000 certified consultants by year-end
summary: OpenAI announced the OpenAI Partner Network on June 14, 2026, its first formal channel program, backed by $150 million and a goal of certifying 300,000 consultants by end of 2026; partners can progress through Select, Advanced and Elite tiers, with specializations in Codex, cybersecurity, APIs and agent transformation, and a new Forward Deployed Experts pilot that puts OpenAI engineers on-site with top-tier partners ahead of a July go-live.

title: OpenAI files confidential IPO at $730B-$850B with Goldman and Morgan Stanley, targets September 2026
summary: OpenAI filed a confidential S-1 with the SEC on June 14, 2026 with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley as lead underwriters, 13 days after Anthropic submitted its own draft; private-market buyers have priced OpenAI at $730-$850 billion on a $122B late-2025 round, analysts expect a >$1T opening-day market cap that would make it one of the five largest IPOs in US history, and the Sept 2026 target sets up a back-to-back public-market test of frontier-AI valuations.

title: White House export ban on Fable 5 and Mythos 5 hits Anthropic days before its IPO
summary: SiliconANGLE reported on June 14, 2026 that the US Commerce Department forced Anthropic to disable Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for every customer globally after the administration, citing 'verbal evidence of a potential narrow, non-universal jailbreak'; Anthropic hit back saying the same standard 'would essentially halt all new model deployments' across the frontier-AI industry, and analysts warned the ban - coming days after Anthropic's confidential S-1 - could derail its $1T-valuation IPO timeline and lose substantial enterprise revenue.

title: Microsoft declares 'AI independence' as MAI-Thinking-1 and MAI-Code-1 replace OpenAI in Copilot and VS Code
summary: Microsoft laid out its AI-independence strategy on June 14, 2026, with Satya Nadella arguing on X that enterprises need to build 'frontier ecosystems' rather than rely on a handful of general-purpose models; the company confirmed the MAI-Thinking-1 reasoning model and MAI-Code-1 (and Code-1-Flash) are now the native engine for GitHub Copilot and VS Code, replacing OpenAI backends at a 10x cost reduction, and Microsoft also unveiled the chip-to-cloud Project Solara stack for agent-first devices built with Qualcomm and MediaTek.

title: Mistral in talks for €3B at a €20B valuation to build its own EU data centers
summary: TechFundingNews reported on June 15, 2026 that Mistral AI has opened early discussions to raise €3 billion at roughly a €20 billion valuation, nearly double the €11.7B mark from its September 2025 Series C; the new round is earmarked for Mistral's first owned data centers, with a target of 1 gigawatt of compute by 2030, ASML's stake would be worth around €2.2B on paper, and the raise follows Mistral's launch of the Vibe agent and physics-AI stack for industrial engineering.

title: Alibaba denies Qwen CTO Zhou Jingren resigned, days after the third Tongyi leader exit of 2026
summary: Alibaba publicly denied on June 14, 2026 a report that Zhou Jingren, CTO of Alibaba Cloud and head of the Tongyi Lab that builds Qwen, had resigned; the company said Zhou continues to lead Tongyi and Qwen development, but the denial comes just six days after he was moved into a new 'Chief Scientist' role overseeing a frontier-AI research institute with no operational responsibility, and is the fourth core Qwen figure to leave in 2026 after Lin Junyang (March) and Yu Bowen, raising fresh questions about leadership stability in China's top open-weights program.

title: Z.ai launches GLM-5.2 with usable 1M-token context and two thinking modes, MIT weights promised next week
summary: Z.ai announced GLM-5.2 on June 13, 2026 as its newest flagship for agentic coding and long-horizon software engineering; the 1M-token context window is now live for all GLM Coding Plan (Lite, Pro, Max, Team) subscribers, the model ships with new High and Max thinking-effort levels, and Z.ai committed to releasing standalone API access, a chatbot on chat.z.ai, and MIT-licensed open weights 'next week' (no exact date confirmed).

title: Google DeepMind maps four routes from human-level AI to superintelligence in 60-page 'AGI to ASI' report
summary: Google DeepMind researchers posted a 60-page 'From AGI to ASI' report to arXiv on June 13, 2026, led by Tim Genewein with co-founders Shane Legg and Marcus Hutter, outlining four overlapping pathways to artificial superintelligence - continued scaling of effective compute (roughly 10x per year for a decade), algorithmic breakthroughs, recursive self-improvement, and large-scale multi-agent coordination - and warning that the field of multi-agent safety 'effectively does not exist yet'.

title: Moonshot open-sources Kimi K2.7-Code, a 1T-MoE coding model with 30% fewer thinking tokens and 12x cheaper than Claude Fable 5
summary: Moonshot AI released Kimi K2.7-Code on June 12, 2026 as an open-source 1T-parameter MoE (32B active) coding model with roughly 30% lower reasoning-token usage than K2.6 and vendor-reported gains of +21.8% on Kimi Code Bench v2, +11.0% on Program Bench and +31.5% on MLS Bench Lite; weights are live on Hugging Face under a Modified MIT license, pricing is $0.95/M input and $4.00/M output (a 12x undercut of the now-suspended Fable 5), and a 6x high-speed variant is due in roughly a week.

title: MiniMax releases M3, a 428B open-weight frontier model with 1M context and native multimodality
summary: MiniMax released the MiniMax M3 open-weights model on June 12, 2026, combining a 428B-parameter mixture-of-experts architecture (23B active) with a 1M-token context window and native image-and-video understanding; the model posts 59.0% on SWE-Bench Pro, 66.0% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 74.2% on MCP Atlas, and ships with the new MiniMax Sparse Attention, a Day-0 API on platform.minimax.io, and weights on Hugging Face under a commercially permissive license.

title: Hugging Face ships Serge, an open-source GitHub-native AI code reviewer that plugs into any OpenAI-compatible model
summary: Hugging Face introduced Serge on June 12, 2026, an Apache-2.0 open-source GitHub-native AI code reviewer that talks to OpenAI-compatible chat-completion endpoints (OpenAI, the Hugging Face Router, local vLLM/TGI/LM Studio) and is already in use on the diffusers, transformers and Serge repositories themselves; reviewers can pick any model exposed by the Hugging Face Router, including freshly open-weighted models like MiniMax M3 and Kimi K2.7-Code.

title: OpenAI Academy launches three enterprise courses - AI Foundations, Applied AI, and Agents and Workflows
summary: OpenAI Academy introduced three new structured enterprise courses on June 12, 2026, with broad coverage on June 15, 2026 - AI Foundations, Applied AI Foundations, and Agents and Workflows - taking employees from basic AI literacy through repeatable prompt workflows to directing agent-assisted work; courses ship with completion certificates, were co-developed with BCG, Accenture and BBVA, and OpenAI says it is the 'beginning of a broader OpenAI Academy learning roadmap' with more role-based paths and organizational reporting planned.

title: OpenAI hit with multi-state probe into possible user harm as its IPO looms
summary: A multi-state coalition of attorneys general served OpenAI with a subpoena on June 12-13, 2026, with widespread coverage on June 15, seeking records on advertising, user engagement and retention, model sycophancy, consumer and health data, and treatment of minors and seniors; OpenAI told reporters it will respond 'constructively' and that today's ChatGPT includes stronger safeguards for minors, and the probe lands just days after OpenAI filed a confidential S-1 with the SEC and hours before rival SpaceX's IPO.

title: Google AI Mode launches information agents for AI Ultra subscribers, proactively tracking topics over time
summary: Google Search VP Robby Stein announced on June 15, 2026 that AI Mode now ships 'information agents' for AI Ultra subscribers across all languages and markets; users can ask the search agent to keep them updated on topics like sneaker drops, concerts, or movie tickets, and the agent will pull from blogs, news sites and social platforms, sending a notification the moment something relevant changes; the feature is the first concrete product from the Search agents Google unveiled at I/O 2026, with AI Pro access planned for later this summer.

title: Google DeepMind, Schmidt Sciences and ARIA open $10M funding call for multi-agent AI safety research
summary: Google DeepMind, Schmidt Sciences, the Cooperative AI Foundation, ARIA and Google.org opened a $10M funding call on June 14-15, 2026 for research into the safety of large populations of AI agents interacting across shared digital systems; Tier 1 grants run up to $300K and Tier 2 grants from $300K to $1M for 1-2 year projects, proposals are due August 8, 2026, and the call follows DeepMind's recent 'distributional AGI safety' paper arguing advanced capabilities may emerge through coordinated agent networks rather than a single monolith.

title: US order to block foreign access to Anthropic's top models marks first AI-specific export-control reversal
summary: The Next Web reported on June 15, 2026 that the US government's June 12 directive to Anthropic is the first export-control measure aimed at specific AI models rather than chips or the hardware that runs them; because the directive targets foreign nationals on a multi-tenant cloud service, the only practical compliance path was to switch the models off globally, and Anthropic says the same standard 'could essentially halt all new model deployments' across the industry if it became the template.

title: 76 cybersecurity experts blast US government for restricting Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos 5
summary: Dozens of prominent cybersecurity CEOs, CISOs, venture capitalists and researchers - 76 signatures as of Monday morning - sent a letter on June 14-15, 2026 to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross criticizing the Trump administration's export-control directive on Anthropic; the letter argues the action 'has taken the best models away from defenders, created market uncertainty, and risked America's AI leadership without any real risk to justify it', and warns that China is 'only months behind the best American models' on cyber capability.

title: xAI upgrades Grok Tasks to Grok Automations with reusable skills, model selector, and live X data
summary: xAI launched Grok Automations on June 15, 2026 as a substantial upgrade from Grok Tasks, introducing reusable skills (prebuilt and bespoke), a model selector that routes each task to the appropriate Grok model, and deep integration with real-time data from X; the launch ships alongside the Grok Build CLI and a marketplace for plugins, and xAI explicitly positions the move away from the cryptocurrency/tokenization path other AI platforms are taking, betting instead on tangible software enhancements.

title: xAI safety lawsuit deepens as Kim complaint cites 23,000 suspected CSAM images, four state probes, and ignored fixes
summary: An AI CERTs News analysis on June 15, 2026 reports that Devin Kim's whistleblower suit against xAI and SpaceX is now part of a broader 'AI Safety Lawsuit' template being filed in Connecticut, California, Baltimore and the UK, citing the same product flaws; the Center for Countering Digital Hate counted 23,000 sexualized child images in 11 days of Grok testing, four US states and one UK jurisdiction have opened formal probes since January 2026, and Moody's has flagged the governance dispute as a credit-watch item ahead of the SpaceX IPO.

title: NVIDIA ships fused MoE MLP kernels that cut DeepSeek-V3 training time 8% and GPT-OSS 93%
summary: NVIDIA published a technical blog on June 15, 2026 describing advanced fused MLP kernels built with the CuTe DSL that target the memory and synchronization bottlenecks of mixture-of-experts training; the kernels ship in the cuDNN Frontend and integrate with Transformer Engine and Megatron Core, delivering 1.3x-2x kernel-level speedups, full-iteration CUDA Graph support, native quantization (MXFP8, NVFP4), and end-to-end training-time improvements of up to 8% on DeepSeek-V3 and 93% on GPT-OSS, with JAX support in development.

title: NVIDIA spotlights 'World-Action Models' as DreamZero tops April 2026 RoboArena ahead of Pi-0.5
summary: NVIDIA's technical blog on June 15, 2026 surveys the rise of World-Action Models (WAMs) - robot foundation models that use pretrained video backbones like Wan and Cosmos to jointly denoise video and action tokens, with NVIDIA's own DreamZero leading the April 2026 RoboArena leaderboard at 1750 points (above Pi-0.5's 1622); the post frames WAMs as a credible alternative to the VLA (vision-language-action) recipe established by Pi-0 and used by NVIDIA GR00T, Xiaomi Robotics and Being-H0.5, and predicts VLA-WAM hybrids as the likely next step.

title: Microsoft Research's Mirage cuts video world-model GPU memory 55x and compute 10x, tops WorldScore
summary: Microsoft Research, Zhejiang University, the University of Adelaide and Monash University posted arXiv preprint 2606.09828 on June 15, 2026 introducing Mirage, a video world model that moves the spatial-consistency memory into the model's latent space rather than keeping it in pixel space; Mirage reaches up to 10.57x faster end-to-end video generation, a 55x smaller VRAM footprint and state-of-the-art WorldScore results, beating the pixel-space point-cloud approach used by Google DeepMind's Genie 3, Runway's GWM-1 and NVIDIA's Cosmos; code is open-sourced on Microsoft's GitHub.

title: Microsoft faces proposed securities class action over Azure and Copilot AI disclosures
summary: The City of St. Clair Shores Police and Fire Retirement System filed a proposed class action in the US District Court for the Western District of Washington on June 12, 2026, with coverage on June 15, alleging Microsoft overstated its AI positioning and understated capacity holdbacks and slower-than-expected Copilot subscription conversions; the complaint says Microsoft's January 28 Q2 FY26 earnings - which showed Azure growth slowing because of computational capacity holdbacks - revealed the misrepresentations, and Bloomberg Law reports the suit also names dealings with OpenAI among the alleged misstatements.

title: Zhipu AI stock rockets 48% as it makes GLM-5.2 open source the same week Anthropic's Fable 5 was banned
summary: South China Morning Post reported on June 15, 2026 that shares of Zhipu AI (trading as Knowledge Atlas Technology) surged as much as 48% to HK$1,620 in Hong Kong morning trade after the company confirmed it would release GLM-5.2 under an MIT open-source license that week; the stock is now up more than 780% since its blockbuster January IPO, the timing undercuts Anthropic's now-banned Fable 5, and the GLM Coding Plan is positioned at roughly a tenth of Claude Code / Claude Max pricing, with full open weights arriving during the week of June 16.
